science.title: Biogenic synthesis of silver nanoparticles using Prosopis farcta: a green nanotechnology approach for enhanced antimicrobial activity
science.description: The green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant extracts provides a non-toxic and sustainable alternative to conventional chemical methods. This study reports the novel biosynthesis of AgNPs using the leaf extract of Prosopis farcta as both a reducing and stabilizing agent. The formation of AgNPs was confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy (200–600 nm). Comprehensive characterization via FT-IR, FESEM, XRD, and DLS revealed that the synthesized nanoparticles were spherical with an average diameter of 39 nm (p < 0.05) and high colloidal stability (zeta potential: -49.7 mV). The antibacterial efficacy of these AgNPs was evaluated against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Results demonstrated potent antibacterial activity, with a concentration of 15.3 µg/mL producing a maximum inhibition zone of 14 ± 0.9 mm against Staphylococcus aureus. This efficacy is comparable to commercial antibiotics such as gentamicin and ciprofloxacin.

science.title: Milky Way-like simulation reveals how central galactic structures grow together
science.description: Understanding the formation and evolution of the centers of galaxies is one of the most intriguing challenges in astrophysics. The new study aims to unveil the physical processes that led to the formation of two striking features surrounding the black holes at the centers of most galaxies: nuclear star clusters and nuclear stellar disks. Only in the last decade have such galactic structures been observed in the Milky Way and extragalactic systems.
